detail.title: What would the requester submit?

blocks.value: A configuration is a set of values the application reads when deciding what to do. A routing table can change a business outcome without a new application build. Start when the purchasing owner proposes a new group for unit B. The configuration owner retrieves the effective production settings and checks them against the reviewed copy before preparing a difference, or diff. A version label alone cannot reveal someone’s unrecorded edit. If the copies differ, record the discrepancy and resolve the baseline before asking QA to test the proposal.

blocks.caption: Illustrative change request, still awaiting review and qualification
rows: Purpose and requester
Purchasing rule maintainer requests that unit B’s eligible submissions go to its successor approver group. The business owner must confirm the intended membership and effective date.
Objects and authority

Prior prod-routing-11; proposed prod-routing-12. Configuration owner prepares the change. Purchasing owner verifies recipients. QA lead verifies test evidence. Authorized release reviewer decides on production use.
Boundary
New requests for unit B, the former and proposed approver groups, requester decision rights, and unit A as the neighboring unchanged unit. Inventory open B requests separately.
Unchanged application
Use the accepted build-418 image and verify its identity in the environment before reusing any application-level evidence.
Work item and state

Open a new Jira change work item, relate it to CC-123, and add web links to the mapping review, test record and disposition. Proposed status: Awaiting review. CC-123 remains Released in the recorded workflow.

blocks.caption: Illustrative proposed mapping diff with invented group names
blocks.value:
--- prod-routing-11 (illustrative excerpt)
+++ prod-routing-12 (proposed excerpt)
 purchasing:
   unit-a: purchasing-a-approvers
-  unit-b: purchasing-b-approvers
+  unit-b: purchasing-b-successor-approvers

The names in this diff illustrate a possible request. The qualification file does not publish the underlying group keys for prod-routing-11. Obtain the approved business list independently, including the former group and one account outside both groups. Read access to the settings and group directory lets the reviewer verify membership. Keep permission to edit configuration and permission to approve the production operation with the assigned roles.

detail.title: Which tests could catch a one-line routing mistake?

blocks.value: The QA lead sets up a representative test revision on the accepted image and loads a test-environment equivalent of the proposed mapping. Record the correspondence between test and production groups and confirm that the same selection rule applies. Plan roughly 30 to 45 minutes for this focused exercise after access is ready. Treat this as an estimate. If a shared default or group-membership rule changes, review affected units and widen the session before declaring the test complete.

blocks.caption: Proposed test sheet; observations and sign-off are pending
rows: Unit B buyer submits a fresh eligible request without naming an approver.
The first assignment is automatic. The actor is the routing rule and the recipient is the authorized successor group.
Case, request, first event, actual actor and recipient, effective configuration and digest.
Requester and former group member independently attempt to decide fresh pending B requests.
Each attempt is denied and each request remains pending. Confirm the former member has no overlapping grant that authorizes the action.
Account role, denial, request state read back after each attempt.
Member of the successor group decides a pending B request.
One authorized decision is recorded.
Actual actor, decision event and resulting state.
A unit A buyer submits under the same candidate.
The first assignment goes to A’s designated group. No manual routing is needed.
Independent expectation, first event and request reference.
Owner inspects requests already assigned before a switch.
Their treatment follows the separately approved business rule. Identify any request needing a deliberate reassignment or preserved decision.
Count, owner and disposition; resolve the policy before rollout if unknown.

blocks.label: Principle
blocks.value: The test checks whether changed settings and existing code deliver the intended behavior together. Verify who actually receives a request and who can act after assignment. Both questions matter when group membership changes.

detail.title: What is approved, and where is it enforced?

blocks.value: The release reviewer compares the exact reviewed diff with the tested configuration and checks the identified image. The example’s acceptance conditions are that the B and A routing checks give the expected first recipients, authorized and denied paths preserve the expected states, and there is a disposition for work in progress. A missing observation, unexplained difference, or absent business authorization keeps the request pending. The earlier uat-82 decision applied to the prior scenario and mapping review. Link it as history and seek a fresh decision on the proposed change.

blocks.label: Tool behavior
blocks.value: In GitHub Actions, a job referencing an environment must satisfy that environment’s configured protection rules before it proceeds. Required reviewers depend on plan and repository visibility; when several people or teams are listed as required reviewers, one approval can release that job. Record distinct business and QA decisions separately if the team requires both.

blocks.label: Team policy
blocks.value: Only the authorized operator applies a reviewed and approved version. Start with controlled exposure, verify the effective settings on the running target, and use a controlled request to check its first recipient. The release reviewer authorizes a larger rollout only after the agreed observations are available.

The proposed implementation record would capture who applied which configuration, the time, target revision, application digest, request and observed group. The accepted production baseline in the teaching record is prod-r42 with prod-routing-11 and digest sha256:041f649df9da0e8f01adbfb779b80fef6aef2fad08edecb62f2de49858ccec5c. A future request should re-read the actual baseline before execution in case a different approved change has occurred.

detail.title: If the proposed group receives the wrong work

blocks.value: The earlier recorded incident shows why the reversal plan includes already-routed work. A controlled purchase request on prod-r41 with prod-routing-10 went to the wrong approver, leading the team to halt exposure. Eight requests needed reconciliation. Seven were reassigned and one authorized decision was retained. The corrected rollout used prod-r42 with prod-routing-11. These observations belong to INC-7. They establish neither deployment nor recovery of the later proposed prod-routing-12.

For a hypothetical prod-routing-12 failure, the first operator action would be to stop expansion and preserve the effective settings and first assignment for the triggering request. Compare expected and actual groups. If the observed wrong recipient is attributable to the changed row, restore the reviewed prod-routing-11 settings under the authorized reversal procedure and verify the version actually serving. Use fresh controlled requests to recheck B, A and decision rights before resuming. If the baseline changed meanwhile, have the configuration owner reconcile it before restoring settings.

Restoring a row affects future lookup decisions. It may leave existing work in the wrong queue. The service owner would list affected requests from the exposure interval, assess decisions already taken, and record each correction or justified retention. On the new Jira change record, link any incident and the observations, then record the hold or reversal and its owner. A mistaken success claim based on a zero backlog conceals misrouting. Counting a proposed restore as a completed rollback conceals whether the active configuration was ever verified.

detail.title: What transfers

blocks.value: Azure App Configuration snapshots can retain immutable sets of selected configuration values, giving an operator a specific version to reference during qualification and recovery. With a different configuration store, retain an equally identifiable prior version and verify the running selection, business authorization and affected requests each time settings change.
